Material Economics (2019). Industrial Transformation 2050 - Pathways to Net-Zero Emissions from EU Heavy Industry. University of Cambridge Institute for Sustainability Leadership (CISL), Cambridge. With Wuppertal Institute and the Institute of European Studies (VUB). No DOI printed.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed page). Scenario study: most numbers are pathway totals or chart bars. Loaded: route CO2 intensities printed as labels (steel Exhibit 2.7 per t steel incl. downstream; clinker Exhibit 4.8 per t clinker); 2050 production costs per route as cost-levelized and abatement costs from Exhibits 2.10 (EUR/t steel incl. downstream 150-200), 3.15 (EUR/t plastics incl. downstream 400), 3.22 (EUR/t ammonia), 4.11 (EUR/t cement), read from the rendered pages (bar labels are printed numbers); energy and flows from text and endnotes (H-DRI 3-4 MWh/t, 61 kg H2/t, EAF 0.45 MWh/t, electrolysis 45 MWh/t H2, SMR ammonia 8.9 MWh gas + 2.1 MWh electricity, electrolytic ammonia 9.1 MWh/t, MTO 1.4 MWh/t, CO2-to-methanol 11 MWh/t, clinker 3.7 GJ/t); chemical-recycling and bio-based route balances (Exhibits 3.11, 3.12) as flows. Price year: not stated anywhere; 2019 used and flagged; discount rate not stated; electrolyser 450 USD/kW (2050) loaded as 2019_USD. Annualised capex components and other bar components went to _other-values (they are not capex per capacity). Traps: steel and plastics costs include downstream processing; Exhibit 3.15 costs are per t plastics and several low-CO2 routes include end-of-life CCS; route rows are whole chains mapped (none) or low. Not loaded: pathway volumes, investment and energy-mix totals, circular-economy lever costs, chart-only bar heights.
